description: BoringStack API — health-at-a-glance stat row, RED panels per route, Node.js runtime detail. Event loop utilisation and lag are the first place to look for Node performance issues — they tell you whether the runtime can dispatch callbacks, which CPU and memory don't.

panels.description:
**What:** fraction of time the Node event loop is busy executing JS (vs idle waiting on I/O). 0.0 = idle, 1.0 = fully saturated.

**Why:** the single most important Node.js health signal. The loop is single-threaded — if it has no headroom, the next traffic burst queues requests no matter what CPU/memory show.

**Watch for:** sustained > 0.7 (orange) = thin margin, investigate. > 0.9 (red) = no headroom, next spike degrades. Common culprits: sync FS calls, large JSON.parse, CPU-bound code that should be a worker thread.
panels.title: Event loop utilization

panels.description:
**What:** the 99th-percentile delay between a Node event-loop callback being *ready* to run and *actually* running.

**Why:** complements ELU — ELU tells you *how busy* the loop is, lag tells you *how late* it's running things. A request gets at least this much added latency tax.

**Watch for:** > 50ms (orange) = users feel it. > 200ms (red) = real performance problem. > 1s = service unresponsive (pages via NodeEventLoopBlocked rule).
panels.title: Event loop lag (p99)

panels.description:
**What:** rate of HTTP 5xx responses per second across all routes (5-min average).

**Why:** the most direct 'is something broken right now?' signal. Any non-zero value means at least one request is failing server-side.

**Watch for:** > 0 (orange) = investigate. > 5/s (red) = real degradation; `ApiServerErrorsHigh` rule should already be paging.
panels.title: 5xx error rate

panels.description:
**What:** total HTTP requests per second across every route (5-min average).

**Why:** baseline that makes the other panels' spikes legible — without a reference for typical traffic, you can't tell whether a per-route spike is unusual.

**Watch for:** a sudden drop to 0 = the API stopped accepting requests (paired with `ApiUnreachable`). Sudden jump = check the per-route panel below for which endpoint and the route-status mix.
panels.title: Total request rate

panels.description:
**What:** 1-minute request rate broken out per route (e.g. `GET /api/v1/users/:id`).

**Why:** shows which endpoints generate traffic and how the mix shifts over time.

**Watch for:** one route dominating = caching / rate-limit review candidate. A route that flatlines unexpectedly = silent client breakage. A stacked-colour shift after a deploy = traffic moved between endpoints.
panels.title: Request rate (per route)

panels.description:
**What:** 95th-percentile request duration per route (5-min sliding window).

**Why:** the route-view of 'what does a slow request look like to a user?'. p95 catches the long tail without being dominated by outliers like p99 sometimes is.

**Watch for:** one route climbing while others stay flat = isolated regression (likely a recent change to that handler). All routes rising together = upstream pressure (DB hot, event loop saturated). Pivot to the Tempo trace for that route to see where the time went.
panels.title: Request latency p95 (per route)

panels.description:
**What:** p50 (orange) and p99 (red) of event-loop dispatch lag over time.

**Why:** the timeseries view of the stat at the top. p99 climbing while p50 stays flat = bursty blocking (an occasional slow query or sync call). Both rising together = sustained pressure.

**Watch for:** p99 > 200ms triggers `NodeEventLoopLagging`. Spike right after a deploy = bad release; spike correlated with traffic = capacity limit; spike with no obvious trigger = check the Tempo trace waterfall for a slow span.
panels.title: Event loop lag (p50 + p99)

panels.description:
**What:** ELU (0.0–1.0) over time, purple area.

**Why:** the leading indicator. Lag tells you the loop *is* falling behind; ELU tells you it's *about* to. Watching ELU climb gives you headroom warning before users feel it.

**Watch for:** sustained > 0.9 = `NodeEventLoopSaturated` will page. A slow upward trend over hours/days = you're outgrowing the host; plan to scale before it bites.
panels.title: Event loop utilization

panels.description:
**What:** process resident set size (RSS — total OS memory) and V8 heap-used over time.

**Why:** detects leaks. RSS that grows in lockstep with traffic = normal; RSS that climbs while traffic flatlines = leak. The gap between RSS and heap = native allocations (Buffers, addons, Bun's own memory).

**Watch for:** RSS approaching the container's memory limit = OOM kill imminent (`docker compose ps` will show `OOMKilled`). Heap as a sawtooth = healthy GC; heap monotonically up = leak. Wide RSS-heap gap that keeps growing = native-side leak.
panels.title: Memory (RSS + heap)

panels.description:
**What:** process CPU rate (1-min average), as a fraction (1.0 = one full core saturated).

**Why:** worth glancing at but **not** the primary Node health signal — see the ELU panels for that. CPU can be high while the loop is healthy (legitimate CPU-bound work in a worker thread) or low while the loop is blocked (waiting on slow I/O).

**Watch for:** sustained 1.0 = a CPU-bound path is monopolising the main thread; consider moving it to a `worker_threads` worker. `HostCpuSaturated` may also be approaching.
panels.title: Process CPU

panels.description:
**What:** stacked request rate grouped by HTTP status code (200, 201, 4xx, 5xx, …).

**Why:** sanity check on the status mix. Most healthy traffic is 2xx; 4xx is the client's fault (bad input, auth); 5xx is yours.

**Watch for:** a sudden 4xx surge after a SPA deploy = client-side regression sending bad payloads. 5xx growth = server-side bug or upstream failure (paired with `ApiServerErrorsHigh`). New 3xx pattern that wasn't there before = intentional redirect or misconfiguration.
panels.title: Requests by status
